incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Dedicated pool capacity alert for tenant 'Orion Therapeutics' in eu-west-1. 95% GPU utilization on pool.orion-dedicated-1 for last 12m, queue depth rising. Severity: P1. Escalation: oncall@eng-sre.
Mira O'Neal: I'm on it, pulling logs + allocation map. ETA 2m.
Alex Huang: Thanks Mira. Noted customer is on Dedicated Reserved contract, burst policy is 'manual-approve'. They have critical inference pipelines.
Samir Patel: Looking at telemetry — we've had a large set of 16-token streaming requests from their batch job hitting simultaneously. Autoscaler didn't trigger because pool is at max_instances (8) for that tenant.
Jess Ramos: @Mira FYI I just pinged Orion TAM. They say some overnight ETL job mis-scheduled and started replaying. They're investigating on their side.
Mira O'Neal: Quick snapshot: 
``` 
pool: pool.orion-dedicated-1
active_instances: 8 (max)
gpu_util: 96.7% avg 10m
queue_depth: 174
pending_requests: 142
recent_scale_events: none
```
Mira O'Neal: Router logs show steady RPS bump at 01:18Z, error rate 0.2% (request timeouts increasing). No model failovers yet.
Lee Carter: Is there any cross-tenant spilling? Are other tenants impacted?
Samir Patel: Isolation looks intact. Other tenants on same host group see normal 10-20% utilization — the scheduling is tenant-isolated. No OOMs.
Kai Morales: If we can't autoscale, we can temporarily allow burst to shared-burst-pool (if policy permits) — but their contract is 'manual-approve' for burst into shared capacity. That requires SOC approval.
Jess Ramos: I'll get legal/compliance signoff ASAP. In the meantime, can we do request-level mitigations? e.g., rate-limit by route or fallback to a smaller model?
Alex Huang: Two quick options: 1) Route new low-priority requests to a quantized model variant (orion-v2-q4) with approximate fidelity. 2) Apply short-term rate-limiting to long-running sync jobs (>=500ms) and prioritize real-time inference.
Mira O'Neal: I can implement a temporary policy on the router to deprioritize requests with header X-job:batch for 15m. Putting the ACL now, will monitor queue.
Samir Patel: Suggest also increasing batching window to 40ms for that pool to increase throughput. Will change kernel settings if Mira confirms.
Mira O'Neal: ACL applied: deprioritize X-job:batch -> moved to low-priority queue. Observing queue depth drop from 174 -> 98 in 3m.
Kai Morales: I can kick an emergency canary of orion-v2-q4 to the pool to take new low-priority requests. Prep: model size 12GB quantized, latency penalty ~20ms.
Alex Huang: Good. Jess, can you confirm with Orion that best-effort degraded quality is acceptable for non-critical pipeline runs?
Jess Ramos: Orion TAM reports they can accept degraded quality for their nighttime ETL, but not for live patient-facing endpoints. They've confirmed the batch job is ETL. They authorize degraded routing for batch.
Mira O'Neal: Implementing model routing: any request with header X-job:batch -> route to orion-v2-q4. Applying now.
Samir Patel: Increasing batching window + kernel tweak applied. Observing gpu_util drop to 82% in live metrics. Queue depth -> 34. Timeouts trending down.
AccountBot: Note: Manual approval required to burst into shared pool. Pending approval from Security and Sales.
Jess Ramos: I'm on the approvals thread with Security (cc: @security) and Sales. Requesting shared-burst for 1 hour, up to 50% additional capacity.
Lee Carter: While approvals in flight, we should prepare rollback plan if performance hits regressions. Also prepare a dedicated capacity split if this becomes recurring — option to split tenant pool across two host groups.
Kai Morales: Preparing the orion-v2-q4 canary: 3 replicas staged, health passing, added to routing for low-priority.
Mira O'Neal: Metrics look stable after routing changes. No customer-visible 5xx spikes on live endpoints. Prelim mitigation success.
Alex Huang: Great. Next steps: 1) Jess to get signed burst approval if needed. 2) Samir + Mira to monitor and decide on manual burst in 15m if utilization >90% again. 3) Engineering to prepare permanent autoscaler parameter change proposal for tenant pockets.
Samir Patel: If we do approve burst, we should limit to shared-burst-pool and set strict eviction policy: earliest-evict = low-priority, max-burst-duration = 60m. I'll draft runtime config changes.
Jess Ramos: Security approved on call for temporary burst (logs retained, KMS policy ok). Sales approved cost offset with Orion. I have signed off for up to 45 minutes.
Mira O'Neal: Initiating manual burst now: adding 4 instances from shared-burst-pool -> expected capacity +50%.
incident-bot: Action logged: manual-burst by Mira O'Neal at 3902469901, source: eng-ops.
Samir Patel: New pool state: active_instances: 12 (8 reserved + 4 burst), gpu_util: 64% within 2m. Queue depth back to single digits. No error increase.
Kai Morales: Canary traffic (low-priority) successfully served by orion-v2-q4. Latency +25ms, accuracy regression within agreed SLA for batch.
Alex Huang: Marking customer impact: Batch ETL degraded to quantized model for ~27m. No live endpoint impact. Severity updated to P1 -> P2 (partial degraded service for non-critical paths).
Jess Ramos: Communicated to Orion: summary + mitigation + expected follow-up. They appreciate fast response.
Lee Carter: Post-incident actions: 1) Propose autoscaler change to respect tenant bursts (allow scaling to 12 instances under predefined conditions). 2) Add router rule templates for X-job header deprioritization. 3) Run a chaos test on scheduled ETL replays for dedicated pools.
Samir Patel: I'll own autoscaler proposal (timeline 2 days). Mira, can you open a runbook PR with the deprioritization steps?
Mira O'Neal: On it — creating runbook PR and linking metrics/graphs.
Alex Huang: Thanks everyone. Closing note: No customer SLA rollback required. Will follow up with postmortem if repeat happens.
AccountBot: Incident closed (manual) by Jess Ramos at 3902471701.
Jess Ramos: Great work team. Filing short post-incident summary for execs.
Kai Morales: Leaving notes on model performance for the postmortem.
Mira O'Neal: Moving to monitoring watch for another 30m, then handoff to next shift.
Alex Huang: Handoff to night-oncall @Mira scheduled at 3902471701.
Mira O'Neal: Handoff acknowledged. :white_check_mark:
